subject: Request: Normalize seller exemption ID and DBA mapping for marketplace invoices
messages:
From: Jason Li <jason.li@marketplace-retail.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounting Ops <acctops@marketplace-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:27 -0800
Subject: Seller permit normalization for marketplace invoices

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. We're finishing up paperwork on our side to clear a handful of Redwood invoices that are currently on hold (invoice 5791 is the one flagged). A snag we're hitting: our sellers operate under multiple DBAs and we submit a single marketplace seller-permit number that the state issued to our platform, but your AP system is matching permit numbers to the legal entity name on file and the invoice payee.

I attached "seller-permit-12345.pdf" (state-issued seller permit showing the marketplace facilitator number). Can you confirm whether Redwood accepts the facilitator permit number in lieu of per-seller resale certificates for states where the marketplace collects and remits? If not, what exact fields do you need so we can normalize our export?

Quick context:
- We are registered as a marketplace facilitator in CA and WA.
- Individual merchants have DBAs that differ from the legal name on our filings.
- Our export currently sends: seller_permit=12345; merchant_dba=ShopLocal; merchant_ein=12-3456789; invoice_payee=Marketplace Retail Co.

What would make the invoice unholdable today? A consolidated state certificate? A merchant-level resale certificate that lists DBA? An explicit written affidavit that the marketplace is responsible for tax?

Appreciate any specific formatting rules (e.g., exact string match for permit numbers, allowable separators, whether we can send "MarketplaceRetail-12345" or you need pure numerics). We need to get this into our billing pipeline today if possible.

Thanks,
Jason Li
Finance Ops
Marketplace Retail Co.

Attachment: seller-permit-12345.pdf (PDF, 2 pages, state-issue)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Li <jason.li@marketplace-retail.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Seller permit normalization for marketplace invoices

Jason —

Thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the state permit. Short answer: we can accept a marketplace facilitator permit in many states, but our current billing validation needs either (A) the permit number to match the invoice payee record exactly, or (B) a documented mapping that ties the facilitator permit to the merchant DBA/legal entity for that invoice.

Specifics from our side:
- System rule: permit string must match the "tax_id" field on the payer profile exactly (case-insensitive, digits and hyphens only). Any prefixed text (e.g., "MRKT-12345") will trigger a mismatch.
- If the facilitator files on behalf of the seller, we need a short PDF (signed) that:
  * states "Marketplace Retail Co. (permit 12345) is responsible for collecting/remitting sales tax for transactions processed on behalf of [merchant legal name], DBA [merchant dba]"
  * includes the merchant legal name, DBA, and the merchant's EIN (if available)
  * is dated and signed by an authorized rep of the marketplace
- Alternatively, for immediate invoice release we can accept: a scanned reseller certificate per merchant OR a signed facilitator affidavit + the CSV mapping (columns: invoice_id, merchant_legal_name, merchant_dba, merchant_ein, permit_number)

Next steps I can take today:
1) If you can upload the signed facilitator affidavit and the CSV to our secure portal (link below), I can triage and clear invoice 5791 within 24 business hours.
2) If you prefer to normalize the permit string, send a sample export (first 50 rows) and we'll provide a normalization script (regex + examples) you can apply before submission.

Portal link for uploads: https://secure.redwood.ai/uploads/tax-evidence (one-time token will be sent)
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/12345 (I flagged the record).

I've CC'd Kim and Marissa — Kim handles billing exceptions and Marissa is our tax ops lead who will confirm state-specific acceptance.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: invoice-5791-pending.pdf (PDF, invoice snapshot)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Li <jason.li@marketplace-retail.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Seller permit normalization for marketplace invoices

Thanks Jason — following up after review with tax ops.

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 09:14 AM Jason Li <jason.li@marketplace-retail.com> wrote:
> Hi Aditya,
>
> Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. We're finishing up paperwork on our side to clear a handful of Redwood invoices that are currently on hold (invoice 5791 is the one flagged). A snag we're hitting: our sellers operate under multiple DBAs and we submit a single marketplace seller-permit number that the state issued to our platform, but your AP system is matching permit numbers to the legal entity name on file and the invoice payee.

Summary of what we need to clear invoice 5791 today:
- A signed facilitator affidavit (PDF) that explicitly names "Marketplace Retail Co." and permit 12345 and states the marketplace collects/remits on behalf of the listed merchants.
- A CSV mapping file (UTF-8, comma delimited) with the following columns: invoice_id, merchant_legal_name, merchant_dba, merchant_ein, permit_number. Please include invoice 5791 in the CSV.

Formatting notes (must match our ingestion rules):
- permit_number: digits only, no spaces or prefixes (e.g., "12345").
- merchant_ein: format must be "NN-NNNNNNN" if available; enter "NA" if not provided.
- invoice_id: must match the invoice number on the PDF exactly (case-sensitive).

Upload steps:
1) Go to https://secure.redwood.ai/uploads/tax-evidence and request a one-time token.
2) Upload the affidavit PDF and the CSV.
3) Send a short confirmation reply to this thread once uploaded and we'll begin clearance.

If you cannot provide a merchant-level certificate, we can temporarily clear the invoice with an internal finance credit subject to a post-receipt verification (we prefer to avoid credits unless absolutely necessary).

Example CSV row for invoice 5791:
5791,"Smith & Sons, LLC","Smith Tools",12-3456789,12345

If you want, we can run a quick normalization script on the sample export you sent and return a cleaned file. Aditya — please coordinate the token request and let me know if we should auto-apply the normalization.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Billing & Collections Manager
Redwood Inference
